subject: Commercial recap: CitadelPay inference economics & procurement path
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@citadelpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial recap: CitadelPay inference economics & procurement path

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned. I’ve kept this focused on the economics and procurement items you asked us to detail.

Summary of pain / goals (from our talk)
- Primary pain: inference cost volatility and slow realtime response for fraud-check flows (peak events spike tokens).
- Goal: get overall unit cost below $0.0015/request (target) while keeping 95th latency under 220ms for the latency-critical path.
- Constraint: internal pilot budget appears capped at ~$40k/month.

Call takeaways / assumptions we used for the estimate
- Expected volume for pilot: ~12M inference calls / month (avg payload ~250 tokens input + 50 tokens output).
- Current third-party spend you quoted: ~$60k/mo for production traffic (no batching, limited KV cache).
- We model two levers: continuous batching (inference batching windows tuned to latency SLO) and KV/prefix caching for repeated user context.

High-level econ readout (pilot projection)
- Baseline (current setup): ~ $60k/mo (as you reported).
- Redwood pilot (6–8 week POC, conservative): with batching + KV caching + one-half precision quantization profile we expect 30–45% token-cost reduction in the production path.
- Expected pilot cost (Redwood-hosted): ~$28k–$38k/mo depending on caching hit-rate; modeled midpoint: $33k/mo (meets your $40k cap).
- Pilot ROI: estimated incremental monthly savings vs current baseline ~$22k/mo -> payback within ~2–3 months after pilot if extrapolated to full roll-out.

Key assumptions to validate
- Cache hit-rate: we assumed 25–35% effective KV/prefix cache for your flows. If hit-rate is <15% that reduces savings materially.
- Batch window (latency budget): we assumed 8–12ms batching windows for non-latency-critical requests and <3ms for the 95th latency path using isolated priority queues.
- Model variant: cost estimate based on an open LLM variant we tested in our bench; switching to a significantly larger model raises token costs ~1.6–2x.

Attachments: I attached the usage sample you emailed and a first-pass pilot SOW draft so procurement can see scope + billing options.

Proposed next steps (quick wins)
1) Procurement call (include procurement@citadelpay.com) — to confirm billing terms (Net-30 vs Net-45), SOC2 evidence, and required contract clauses.
2) Pilot SOW review — we’ll update SOW to include a capped monthly spend profile that keeps you inside $40k for the pilot.
3) Technical check — brief runbook for cache keys and latency SLAs; we’ll provide a sample config for your infra team.

If these look right I can: (a) update the SOW to add a capped-pilot budget option and (b) schedule the procurement + technical sync. What timing works for you?

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@citadelpay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@citadelpay.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial recap: CitadelPay inference economics & procurement path

Thanks Naomi — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we loop procurement: 

- That cache hit-rate assumption (25–35%) — can you share two concrete scenarios (conservative 15% and optimistic 40%) with the corresponding cost numbers for the pilot? Our traffic is bursty and I want to understand downside.
- For batching: the fraud-check path is very latency-sensitive. Any change that increases 95th latency beyond 220ms is a non-starter. Please flag which parts of the estimate depend on relaxed latency budgets.
- Procurement: we tend to require Net-30 and SOC2 Type II; also need a brief data flow diagram showing where data is stored/transient.

I’m looping procurement on this thread — they’ll confirm the exact contract channel and NDA needs. Can you also provide an example invoice/billing snapshot we can show finance to validate forecasting?

— Daniel
Daniel Ortiz, Sr. Product Manager — Risk
Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@citadelpay.com>

- Billing: we support Net-30 standard. We can also provide a capped-month pilot invoice option (single monthly charge with usage true-up) that fits your $40k limit.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II report and a one-page data flow diagram will be attached to the contract packet.
- Procurement next step: propose a 30-minute call Friday 11:00am PT to walk SOW and billing options. If that works procurement@citadelpay.com please confirm.

Hannah — looping you to help fast-track legal redlines if procurement requests small clause edits.

Thanks Daniel — answers inline and updated next steps.

> Daniel: can you share scenarios for 15% and 40% cache hit and corresponding pilot costs?
- Yes — Ben/Naomi will send a short sensitivity table Monday that shows three lines: conservative (15% hit), base (25–35%), optimistic (40%). We’ll include token-cost assumptions per model tier.

> Daniel: anything that raises 95th >220ms is non-starter
- Understood. Our proposal segments requests by priority queue: fraud checks (priority) routed to isolated low-latency pools with minimal batching (<1–2ms windows). The cost model isolates that traffic so savings come primarily from batching non-critical flows + caching. We’ll mark the savings attribution clearly so you can see what’s safe to apply to the fraud path.

> Daniel: procurement needs Net-30, SOC2, data flow diagram, invoice example
- Confirmed. Attached: updated SOW (redwood_pilot_sow_draft.pdf) with a capped-pilot billing option and a sample invoice snapshot. I’ve also attached the usage sample you sent (citadelpay_usage_sample.csv) for our modeling. SOC2 Type II and data flow one-pager will be added to the packet Ben mentioned.

Proposed immediate next steps
- Monday: Ben + Naomi send conservative/optimistic cost scenarios and a short sensitivity table for cache hit vs batch window.
- Friday 11:00am PT: Procurement + Naomi + Ben (30 min) to review SOW and billing. procurement@citadelpay.com — please confirm availability.
- I’ll update the SOW to include the capped-pilot option and upload a DocuSign preview to the link below.
